trust_decision.summary: Decided in Concurrent::AtomicReference#compare_and_set (the AtomicNumericCompareAndSetWrapper mixed into the Mutex and C-extension backends): when the expected value is Numeric the loop compares with `old == old_value`, and NaN is never == to itself, so _compare_and_set is never attempted and every CAS-based retry (update/try_update/try_update!) never terminates. The published fix adds an explicit `nan?` branch to that one module; it does not touch the JRuby Java numeric CAS or AtomicMarkableReference's own numeric compare.

landing_point.why: The summary names AtomicReference#update livelocking on Float::NAN; this `true until compare_and_set(old_value = get, new_value = yield(old_value))` line is where the symptom is produced. The next hop is the compare_and_set it calls, lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/atomic_reference/numeric_cas_wrapper.rb:17, where the == comparison drops the NaN case.

fix_sites.entry_point: Concurrent::AtomicReference#compare_and_set (alias #compare_and_swap); reached by #update / #try_update / #try_update! (lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/atomic_reference/atomic_direct_update.rb:10-35), Concurrent::Atom#swap (lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/atom.rb:157-170), Synchronization::Object attr_atomic generated update_<name> (lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/synchronization/object.rb:105-111) and Tuple#compare_and_set (lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/tuple.rb:69-73)
fix_sites.module_kind: internal mix-in module (AtomicNumericCompareAndSetWrapper) shared by MutexAtomicReference and CAtomicReference

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: ext/concurrent-ruby/com/concurrent_ruby/ext/AtomicReferenceLibrary.java:117-144 (compareAndSetNumeric), selected as Concurrent::AtomicReference#compare_and_set on JRuby by lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/atomic/atomic_reference.rb:28-34, which includes AtomicDirectUpdate but not AtomicNumericCompareAndSetWrapper

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Both remaining sites are easy to argue away: the Java numeric CAS is JRuby-only code in another language under ext/ that never loads on the MRI box the specs run on, and AtomicMarkableReference is a different class whose value+mark payload is compared its own way, so a solver can say the advisory covers AtomicReference#update and stop after the one Ruby hunk.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Numeric CAS must keep using value equality (==) rather than identity/eql?, so a stored Integer 1, 1.0, 2**100, Rational(1,3) or Complex(1,2) still matches an equal-but-different object (exercised at spec/concurrent/atomic/atomic_reference_spec.rb:128-144), and a NaN expected value must still fail against a non-NaN stored value. A fix that compares with eql?/equal?, or that accepts NaN as matching anything, breaks one or both.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/atomic_reference/numeric_cas_wrapper.rb:17; identity semantics of the backend at lib/concurrent-ruby/concurrent/atomic_reference/mutex_atomic.rb:45-54

O6_input_shapes: Float::NAN as the expected/old value while the stored value is also NaN (the reported shape; must now succeed)
Float::NAN expected while the stored value is a non-NaN Numeric (must stay a failed CAS; fix.diff:61-69 asserts this)
non-NaN Numerics: Integer, Bignum, Float with non-idempotent representation, Rational, Complex, compared with ==
Numeric expected value while the stored value is not Numeric (returns false before the loop body)
non-Numeric expected value: identity path via _compare_and_set, unchanged by the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AtomicReference#update on JRuby: JavaAtomicReference includes only AtomicDirectUpdate, so compare_and_set is the Java compareAndSetNumeric loop, whose `!currentNumber.equals(expectedValue)` returns false for NaN forever, so the Ruby #update loop still hangs after this fix
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: JRuby-only; the numeric wrapper is a Ruby mixin and the JVM class already implements its own numeric CAS, so a solver can call it a separate implementation outside the Ruby fix (and it cannot be exercised on MRI)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file's implementation selector, then a Java source in the ext/ package tree

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AtomicMarkableReference#update: its own loop retries on compare_and_set, which returns false for a Numeric expected value via `expected_val == curr_val`, so a stored Float::NAN livelocks; try_update returns nil and try_update! raises for the same reason
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A different class holding a frozen [value, mark] array with its own numeric-vs-identity comparison rule; the advisory names AtomicReference#update, so the markable reference reads as a neighbouring feature rather than a route into the same sink

O8_uncovered_routes.route: TruffleRuby backend: TruffleRubyAtomicReference includes only AtomicDirectUpdate and inherits compare_and_set from TruffleRuby::AtomicReference, so the NaN equality rule is wherever that class implements it and is not covered by the Ruby wrapper
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Non-MRI engine, implementation lives outside this repository, so it is unverifiable and easy to leave alone
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file's implementation selector; implementation is out of tree

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A float-capable AtomicFixnum (or a numeric CAS helper next to it) whose update retries on `@value == expect.to_i`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: AtomicFixnum already has a compare-and-set plus an update that takes a block; widening it to accept non-integer numerics is a natural change and would reproduce the NaN inequality with the same retry shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An attr_atomic numeric field (generated compare_and_set_<name>/update_<name>) used for a floating-point threshold or average, whose update retry inherits the wrapper's equality rule
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: attr_atomic is the framework's main way to build new concurrency primitives; a numeric attribute is a one-line addition for a maintainer and immediately reaches the same sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An Atom variant (or a swap-adjacent helper) with its own retry loop and a validator, bypassing compare_and_set_value
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Atom#swap already sits next to compare_and_set and shares the pattern; a specialised numeric atom that skips the validator path would be a believable refactor that the wrapper would not cover.

O9_family: CWE-835 loop with unreachable exit condition: CAS retry loop proves equality with `==`, which a stored NaN can never satisfy, so #update never returns

O10_build.language: Ruby (optional C extension for MRI, optional Java extension for JRuby)
O10_build.toolchain: Ruby + Bundler; rspec ~>3.7 and timecop in the :testing group; rake + rake-compiler build concurrent-ruby-ext, which is optional because the loader falls back to the pure-Ruby MutexAtomicReference
O10_build.project_tests: spec/concurrent/atomic/atomic_reference_spec.rb holds RSpec shared examples run against AtomicReference, MutexAtomicReference and CAtomicReference (plus JavaAtomicReference / TruffleRubyAtomicReference on those engines); spec/concurrent/atomic/atomic_markable_reference_spec.rb covers the markable sibling (update retry at :80-90, numeric compare at :109-137). Run with `bundle exec rspec spec/concurrent/atomic`.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Special-case NaN in AtomicDirectUpdate#update itself (e.g. `return new_value if old_value.nan?`) or switch the numeric compare to eql?/equal?, leaving compare_and_set, try_update/try_update!, the JRuby Java loop and AtomicMarkableReference untouched.
